newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania refinancing credits 8.4 pct up in July.
newsitem.headline: Romania refinancing credits 8.4 pct up in July.

text.p: Romania's central bank refinancing loans went up by 8.4 percent in July, when Lombard loans surged to 1.6 trillion lei from 260.2 billion in June, National Bank (BNR) data showed.
Total daily refinancing was 4.7 trillion lei on average in July, when the BNR's support for farmers exceeded 1.0 trillion lei, rising 7.2 percent from June.
Auctioned credits reversed a five-month dip, rising to 467.1 billion lei in July from 358.5 billion in June, while structural loans stayed almost flat at 1.07 trillion lei.

After several months of gains special loans dropped sharply to 516.9 billion in July from 1.72 trillion in June as the central bank, fighting inflationary pressure, cut support to two troubled private banks in mid-July.

The BNR had extended special credits to keep afloat Banca Dacia Felix SA and Renasterea Creditului Romanesc Credit Bank SA after they revealed big debts and losses. Courts are expected to rule on their fate -- reorganisation or winding up.
Average annual interest rates charged for each type of BNR's refinancing windows were 35 percent for structural loans, 49 percent for one-week funds and 90 percent for Lombard.
Special credits had 45 percent interest in July and support for farmers carried an annual 29.5 percent. -- Mirela Eremia, Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
